children: Sri Lanka's Ceylon Petroleum Corp is scouting for a joint venture partner as it plans to double refining capacity to 100,000 barrels per day within four years, Managing Director Mayura Neththikumarage said on Tuesday.

"This will help us achieve fuel supply security," Neththikumarage told Reuters on the sidelines of the APPEC industry conference, referring to global tightness in oil products markets due to the U.S.-Iran war.
Sri Lanka currently imports transport fuel from Singapore, Malaysia, South Korea and India, he said.
The company will issue a request for proposal within two months for the joint venture and expects to move quickly to the expansion stage, he said.
CPC is diversifying its crude sourcing and is testing Saharan blend oil. It already uses U.S. West Texas Intermediate and Russia's Siberian Light crude, Neththikumarage said.
The refiner imported 90,000 metric tons of WTI in May, he added.
